predecessors.name: Kingdom of Italy
predecessors.text: the Veronese march with Trentino, Friuli and Istria

successors.name: Holy Roman Empire
successors.text: the cities of the Veronese League of 1164: Verona, Padua and Vicenza (Venice is left out)

ledger.x: 952: Berengar II gives up the Veronese march at Augsburg.
952: the march is held by the dukes of Bavaria.
976: the march becomes a Carinthian march (same sentence as above; the rulers list gives Henry III the Younger 976-978).
1004: Henry II gives the Adige valley around Trento to the bishops of Trent.
1070: Istria is again a march of its own.
1077: Friuli around Aquileia leaves the march.
1151: Conrad III takes the march from the duke of Carinthia.
1151: Conrad III 'finally divested Duke Henry V of Carinthia of the remaining Veronese march and enfeoffed Margrave Herman III of Baden'.
1167: the Lombard League is formed and the march ends in fact.

wars.name: Lombard League war against Frederick Barbarossa
wars.outcome: The Veronese League of 1164 merged into the Lombard League of 1167 (oath of Pontida, 7 April 1167); the emperor's army was defeated at Legnano on 29 May 1176; the Peace of Constance of 1183 compromised.

certainty.note: The page names the march's parts but fixes no border; the Adige valley grant of 1004 and the 1070 and 1077 detachments are dated, their frontiers are not.
